body:
After merging the [most recent changes from WebFPSci](https://github.com/NVlabs/WebFPSci/pull/1) this branch now supports additional parametrization of all experiment parameters from the URL. This should reduce the need for things like additional experiment modes in the future. 

We will still support `mode=easy`  to give a compact way to reduce experiment difficulty for now, though the same change could now be supported with `targetMinSize=1&targetMaxSize=2&targetMinSpeed=8&targetMaxSpeed=10`.

I just gave this a shot, but increase `targetMinSize` to 2 and `targetMaxSize` to 3 and got the following results: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26633010/120562808-291aba80-c3d5-11eb-9aed-c371db5b7a4d.png)

I feel like the size 1 targets may still be a little too small for easy, but the size 3 targets are probably larger than we'd need given that quite a few targets seem to spawn close to the user.  I also find it weird that the "normal" max size is 3, but easy mode sets the max size smaller than that.

It's probably worth doing some tests or reviews to see what we think might be the best setting for "normal" and "easy". As a quick proposal, maybe 2-2.5 is a good "easy" range and 0.5-2 would be a good "normal" range. 

Another thing I noticed (but should probably be a separate PR/issue) is that sometimes the target respawning and motion ends up moving the aim very high. This makes aiming harder and a bit more annoying.

@jspjutNV I'll plan to make a commit to increase the target size to the range suggest (2-2.5 easy and 0.5-2 normal). I assume you are okay with the speed ranges being used.

I think the target spawn mechanics could be improved a bit in general in WebFPSci. Currently we spawn the target relative to the current view direction over a (uniformly randomized) azimuth/elevation range; however, it may make more sense to improve this mechanic to:
- Use an annual region to avoid spawning targets at near 0 azimuth _and_ elevation relative to the current view direction
- Bias targets towards the horizon when the view elevation starts to grow high/low

I'll go ahead and create an issue/branch in WebFPSci to help deal with this.

Quick side note, after playing with this a bit I'll probably use 0.5-1.5 for the "normal" mode targets, even a size 2 target seems a bit "too easy" now that we support an explicit easy mode and narrower range of target size should provide more consistent results between conditions.
